The core operation involves classifying software repositories by license type to determine legal reimplementation scope. The system uses a binary compliance check (C) derived from license classification (L), where L ∈ {MIT, BSD, First-Party} implies C=True. Signals in the 47-registry are evaluated for compatibility with this compliance. A shadow weight Z is assigned such that Z=0 when C=False. This creates a dual logic: one for access control (L→W) and another for signal activation (C→Z). Failure modes occur when L is ambiguous or missing, leading to undefined W and Z values. The system must maintain consistency between license evaluation and registry signal assignment to avoid leakage of restricted code into legal frameworks.
